messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up to the service-auth RFC — proposal: make the default key shape 'project-scoped + role-hint' (lightweight token). Rationale: simpler runtime checks, aligns with most ingest/read paths.
Alex: Can you sketch how cross-project proxies (ingest pipelines, backfills) work? They often need org-level access today.
Maya: Good point. Idea is to allow a special 'proxy' client flow: proxy gets a scoped umbrella token that can mint per-project ephemeral sub-tokens using a constrained exchange. Umbrella tokens are tightly audited.
Sam: How does this affect RBAC? We need a clear mapping: API key -> claims {project, roles, origin} and runtime checks -> role-bitset. Minimal extra DB lookups.
Priya: I worry about migration: we currently have org-scoped API keys in a lot of infra. Can we do a compatibility shim?
Maya: Plan: shadow-emit for 4 weeks, then transform layer that accepts org-keys and returns equivalent project-scoped claims for services that are still on old code paths. No silent drops.
AuthBot: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/service-auth-lightweight-v2 — summary posted in doc (auto).
Alex: Excellent. For the umbrella proxy flow, we must limit TTL and scoping. TTL <= 10m for minted sub-tokens? Also rate-limit minting per umbrella.
Priya: Agreed on TTL. Also add a hard cap on number of active sub-tokens per umbrella to limit blast radius.
Sam: Sample introspect shape I'd expect from token introspection API:

```
{
  "token": "abc...",
  "claims": {
    "project": "proj-123",
    "roles": ["ingest","read"],
    "origin": "umbrella:proj-999",
    "exp": 1710000000
  }
}
```

Keep claims tiny — arrays short, role enums compact.
Maya: On telemetry/audit: emit event with fields {actor, token_kind, project, origin, action, decision}. We can backfill from access logs during the shim period.
Alex: Implementation detail: put origin_project in the signed claim so runtime can enforce without DB. For policy updates, push a small policy cache keyed by project id.
Priya: Perf note: avoid per-request policy fetch. Use local cache + async refresh. Also prefer encoded role-bitset in claim so check is a single mask op.
Sam: Example check in pseudocode: `if (claims.role_mask & REQ_ROLE_INGEST) { allow } else { deny }` — no JSON parsing on hot path.
Maya: OK — action items: (1) Priya + Alex: design shim & umbrella minting limits, (2) Sam: finalize claim shape (compact), (3) Platform: add audit event schema, (4) Eng-owners: plan canary rollout for 3 services. We'll sync T+2 days.
Alex: thumbs-up. One more ask: add a migration FAQ for customers referencing org keys.
Priya: Will draft FAQ. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks all — will add notes to the RFC and send a short RFC patch tonight.
AuthBot: Noted — follow-up: issue created https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-3210 (auto).
